question: Should OpenClaw core accept a persisted, user-configured OTLP diagnostics surface and shared instrumentation API now, before a broader instrumentation plan exists?
rationale: The implementation is opt-in and bounded, but it establishes a permanent core configuration and privacy contract whose acceptance requires maintainer intent beyond mechanical correctness.

options.title: Accept bounded groundwork
options.body: Approve the probe-only endpoint and shared helpers after the delivery-state defect is fixed and refreshed current-main validation passes.

options.title: Keep docs and defer runtime
options.body: Retain the telemetry boundary design but defer packages, settings, UI, and helper APIs until a concrete instrumentation use case is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded groundwork
recommendation.body: Approve the probe-only endpoint and shared helpers after the delivery-state defect is fixed and refreshed current-main validation passes.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing diagnostics/settings surface and its test baseline trace most strongly to their merged history.
